name: Class alias editing is unvalidated
answer:
ALIASES MUST BE NON-EMPTY AND TRIMMED; DUPLICATES ARE ALLOWED BUT WARNED; AND A DISPLAY MARKER MUST NEVER REACH A FILE.

The question asks whether aliases must be unique, non-empty, and defined once per project. Three parts, and they do not all go the same way.

NON-EMPTY: yes. An empty alias is indistinguishable from no alias in every export - both write the class id as the name - so accepting one lets a user believe they have named a class when they have not. An alias that is only whitespace is the same case. Trim, and treat the result as no alias rather than as an alias that happens to be blank.

UNIQUE: no, but warn. Two classes called 'car' is almost certainly a mistake, and it makes the COCO categories block ambiguous and the VOC and CreateML files unreadable as a class map. But refusing the edit is worse than reporting it: a user renaming class 3 to 'car' before renaming class 1 away from 'car' would be blocked mid-way through a legitimate change. Accept it, mark both rows, and say what it costs.

DEFINED ONCE PER PROJECT: no - decision 6 keeps aliases per image. Same answer as RULE-007 and RULE-014, same reason.

THE DEFECT IS THE URGENT PART AND IS NOT A PRODUCT CHOICE. The card records that the active-class display marker can leak into a saved label. A marker is a UI affordance; if it can reach a file, then what the user sees and what they export have diverged, and the export is wrong in a way nothing reports. The rewrite must keep the stored alias and its presentation in separate values - the store holds what the user typed, the view decorates it - so there is no code path by which decoration can be persisted. That is structural, not a validation rule, and it is the fix worth making.
